claims.claim: Listed change-state options: vehicles {4 concealment, 5 half speed} or {5}; infantry {2 and 3 charge, 4 concealment}; option 0 (normal) and option 1 (march) were never listed for any unit
Action 6 is listed only for units without a move path: stationary units (stop 1) and units in the move-to-stop transition; never for a unit with a move path
A suppressed vehicle is listed half speed only, never concealment, consistent with the rule that suppression prevents concealment (D4)
Action 6 is listed in every deployment decision; whether a change ordered during deployment, while cur_step stands still, completes before play is unknown

move_state is 0 for every listed own unit, never changes, and change_state_remain_time is never positive: no state transition occurs in any record, so no transition duration, speed or observation effect is observed
The documented unit field target_state is absent from every unit record read; every other field the audit reads is present
claims.level: DIRECTLY OBSERVED (CONTRADICTED for the documentation's field list)

claims.claim: Entering concealment takes 75 s, during which the unit executes no other command; a tank firing interrupts it; suppression prevents or interrupts it; once concealed, moving or firing ends it at no time cost
A concealed unit is observed at half distance (not for a vehicle lower than its observer) and is a favourable target in the direct- and indirect-fire tables

March: vehicles only, on a road hex, after locking weapons; 75 s to enter and to leave; no fire, embarking or leaving the road while marching; blocked by a stopped or non-marching unit in the next hex; the largest adverse target modifier
March hex time 8 s per unit of march cost (90 km/h on a 200 m hex, cost defined relative to the mode's maximum speed)
Charge doubles or quadruples infantry speed and adds one fatigue level per charged hex; second-level fatigue stops movement; no transition time is documented
Half speed (option 5) has no documented effect other than crossing minefields
Whether and when option 1 (march) is listed, e.g. after a lock on a road hex
Action 10 is listed only for units with a non-empty move path, ground and air, traversing or waiting; never for a unit without a path
At the natural end of a path (no stop order) stop becomes 1 exactly 75 steps after the move path empties, in every arrival observed to settle; movement is listed again at once (a normal stop)
claims.scope: H0, H1, H2 arrivals that settled

claims.claim: After an arrival, infantry fighting vehicles and other non-tank units list a shoot option only from 75 steps on; tanks list it at once (they fire while moving, D8)
claims.scope: arrivals with a later shoot listing

claims.claim: A stop issued to a unit waiting in front of a full hex is echoed without error, sets flag_force_stop one step later, withdraws every listed action and is deferred while the next hex stays full
The effect of a stop on a traversing unit: completes its hex, then a 75 s penalty transition during which it takes no action (D6)
speed above 0 does not exclude a unit traversing towards a hex that fills before it arrives (448 such unit-steps in the Sprint 2 split game)
Action 11 is listed only for stationary vehicles (stop 1, no path) with unfolded weapons that are not suppressed, never in the move-to-stop transition, never for infantry or aircraft
Every listed own unit's weapon_unfold_state is 1 (unfolded) throughout; action 12 is never listed; no lock or unfold occurs in any record
The observation holds one lock state per unit (weapon_unfold_state, weapon_unfold_time), so per-weapon states cannot be represented; whether the engine keeps them per weapon is unknown
Locking and unfolding take 75 s each and exclude other commands; locking is required before march and unfolding after march before firing
Lock and unfold are listed in the deployment stage too (11: every deployment decision)
